## 5. Worst setup paths in plain words

The tool gives start, end and slack only (no per-cell delays), so dominant cells cannot be named from this data.

1. **`clk_div[6]` -> `_813_`, slack 8.9381 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60)**; also 8.9549 ns (nom_ss) and 8.9716 ns (min_ss). This is the worst setup path in the design. It starts at the `clk_div[6]` input port (input delay 6.0 ns, driven by an inv_2 model) and ends at internal flop `_813_`. By the spec, clk_div is latched at start and compared with 4 (N = max(clk_div,4)), so this is most likely the clamp/compare and load logic feeding the divider register. It is worst at the slow corner because cell delays grow at 1.60 V / 100C. The related path `clk_div[6]` -> `_812_` has 9.2624 ns (nom_ss) and 9.281 ns (min_ss).
2. **`start` -> `_819_`, slack 9.2184 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60)**. Starts at the `start` port (input delay 6.0 ns), ends at flop `_819_`; this is the start-accept / parameter-latch enable logic. In the ff corners `start` -> `_818_` appears with 12.4111 ns (nom_ff), 12.4424 ns (min_ff), 12.3856 ns (max_ff).
3. **`miso` -> `_764_`, slack 9.7879 ns (nom_tt), 9.7817 ns (min_tt), 9.7955 ns (max_tt), 9.7938 ns (nom_ff), 9.789 ns (min_ff), 9.7999 ns (max_ff)**. Starts at the asynchronous `miso` port with the spec's 10.0 ns input delay (REQ-022) and ends at `_764_`, which I take to be the first flop of the 2-flop synchronizer. The path is short; most of the budget is consumed by the 10 ns input delay itself, so this path is worst only in tt/ff corners where internal logic paths are fast. REQ-022 (setup slack >= 0 on IO paths) is met by this data.

All worst setup paths are input-port-to-flop paths; slack is dominated by the SDC input delays (6.0 ns and 10.0 ns) rather than by internal logic. No flop-to-flop path appears among the reported worst paths.

## 6. Hold

- Hold slack is positive in every corner. Worst: 0.104 ns (min_ff_n40C_1v95), 0.1058 ns (nom_ff), 0.1076 ns (max_ff). Under the gating 10% derate: 0.0571 ns (min_ff), 0.0584 ns (nom_ff), 0.0598 ns (max_ff).
- This is post-CTS signoff data, so the hold check is the required one (hold after CTS). Hold endpoints are not in the tool data; a min-path report for the ff corners is needed to name them.

## 7. Ranked fixes (only hold margin is thin; setup needs no fix)

No fix is required to meet the current targets. If a larger hold guard band is wanted at the ff corners, in order of expected effect:

1. **Targeted hold-buffer insertion on the hold-critical endpoints at ff corners** (OpenROAD repair_timing -hold with a positive hold margin). Most direct: adds delay only on the short min paths. Setup cost is negligible because setup slack is at least 8.9381 ns everywhere.
2. **Delay cell on short flop-to-flop paths found in the ff min-path report** (for example shift-register and synchronizer stage-to-stage connections, which are typically the shortest paths in this design). Same effect as (1) but chosen by hand per path.
3. **Reduce clock skew on the CTS leaf buffers** by re-running CTS with a lower max fanout per buffer (bringing clkbuf_3_*__f_clk/X from 11-17 toward the SDC limit 10). This also removes the max-fanout findings, but its effect on hold is indirect and could go either way; verify with a re-run.
4. **Re-placement** of launch/capture flop pairs on hold-critical paths is the weakest lever here and is not recommended unless (1)-(3) are insufficient.

Any change must be confirmed by a fresh OpenSTA run on all 9 corners; no result above is claimed beyond what reports/sta_tool.json shows.
